description:
FILED s510 (Fable, 2026-10-06) after brian d foy\x27s reply on r/perl ("how do you know rand takes one argument? I can redefine it" -- his blog post "Get real random numbers from Perl\x27s rand()" replaces rand and adds a list context).  Probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/foy/*.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main b06f833a-era.

WHAT IS RIGHT TODAY (ir-spec 7.1a, #1870/#1992): the replacement IS called for `use subs`, a `use M qw(NAME)` import list, `BEGIN { *CORE::GLOBAL::NAME = sub {...} }` and `BEGIN { package Other; *main::NAME = sub {...} }`; a plain `sub rand {...}` does not displace the built-in (b-plain-sub.pl, as perl); `use Time::HiRes qw(time sleep)` works (f-hires.pl); a replacement WITH a prototype is parsed by it (`use subs "length"; sub length (\@)` -- g-proto-override.pl); his own usage `my @a = rand(100)` with a list-context replacement works (i-wantarray.pl row 1).

THREE GAPS, all silent:
 1. THE PARSE (a-subs.pl, d-core-global.pl, e-glob-begin.pl, h-later-def.pl): `$, = "|"; print rand 5, sin 4, rand sin 1, 2, 3;` with a prototype-LESS replacement
      perl: myrand(5,-0.756802495307928,myrand(0.841470984807897,2,3))        (a user sub without a prototype is a LIST operator)
      PCL : myrand(5)|-0.756802495307928|myrand(0.841470984807897)|2|3        (the built-in\x27s named-unary rule is kept)
    With parentheses the two agree, which is how a stand-in for a built-in is normally called -- so the exposure is a paren-less call followed by more list items.  The fix belongs where the term rule is chosen: once `builtin_override_target` answers for a name, the argument rule is the REPLACEMENT\x27s prototype (none = list operator), not Config\x27s entry for the built-in.  CORE::GLOBAL: perl parses by the override\x27s prototype too (probe before assuming).
 2. A DEFAULT-EXPORT override (c-import.pl): `use MyRand;` where MyRand.pm has `our @EXPORT = qw(rand)` -- perl calls MyRand::rand, PCL calls the BUILT-IN.  The override is decided from the `use` statement\x27s own import list; a `use` with NO list takes the module\x27s @EXPORT, which PCL already reads for prototypes.  docs/not-supported.md lists only the `BEGIN { M->import }` spelling (#2053); this one is not written down.
 3. CONTEXT for a CORE::GLOBAL replacement (i-wantarray.pl): `my $x = rand(1)` inside a sub called in list context -- the replacement\x27s `wantarray` is UNDEF (void) where perl says scalar (false but defined).  The `use subs` spelling is right (j-subs-wantarray.pl: an ordinary sub call with its context bind).  So the CORE::GLOBAL route reaches the user code without a scalar bind.

LINK to #2775 (the list-context bind around built-ins): a REPLACED built-in is user code that reads `wantarray`.  In a LIST slot it gets list context today only through that fallback bind -- the analysis job must cover overridden built-ins before the bind is removed (added to its brief, section B).

SIZE: not scheduled.  Gap 1 is the one foy\x27s example hits; 2 is a plausible real import (a module that exports a drop-in `rand` / `sleep` / `time` by default); 3 is a corner.

=== SHARPENED the same hour, from foy's actual program (stackoverflow.com/a/4093822; foy/k-foy-so.pl = his code with a counter in place of random.org; foy/l1.pl .. l5.pl) ===
Gap 1 is NOT only the paren-less parse.  WITH parentheses and WITH a prototype on the replacement the call still carries the built-in's one-argument rule, and a parenthesised list collapses to its LAST value:
   *CORE::GLOBAL::rand = sub (;$$) {...}   rand(undef, 5)   rand(1, 2)   my @a = rand 5, 5
      perl:  g(undef,5)   g(1,2)   1 value g(5,5)
      PCL :  g(5)         g(2)     1 value g(5)
   the same with no prototype, with `use subs qw(rand); sub rand (;$$)`, with `use subs` and no prototype (l2, l3, l4), and for other one-argument built-ins: `sleep(1, 2)` -> slept(2), `hex("ff", 16)` -> hex(16) (l5).  A replacement called with the built-in's OWN argument count is right (`rand(7)`, `rand()`, `time + 1`, `hex "a"`).
So: every override spelling reaches the replacement, and none of them hands it more arguments than the built-in takes.  foy's program (a `rand` that takes a second argument = how many numbers) prints different numbers in every block.  FIX SITE (not read): where the call's argument list is built for a name whose `builtin_override_target` answers -- the argument rule and the argument LIST must be the replacement's (its prototype, else a plain list), exactly as for any user sub.

=== FIX SITE, READ (Fable, same session; USER asked "can we even fix that?" -- YES for every replacement the compiler already sees) ===
The override registry is filled BEFORE any expression is parsed (Parser2 `_premerge_builtin_overrides($doc)`, ~line 1560: `use subs`, import lists, `*CORE::GLOBAL::NAME` and `*Other::NAME` assignments, each with its line and column) and it is position-aware (`Pl::Environment::builtin_override_target($pkg, $name, $line, $col)`).  It is CONSULTED only at code generation (Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~2316: `force_user = 1`), after Pl/PExpr.pm has parsed the call with the BUILT-IN's argument rule -- which it reads from `known_no_of_params` directly in about twelve places (PExpr.pm 3008, 3044, 3442, 3805, 4721, 4790, 4876, 5398, 5478, 5887, 5892; Parser2.pm 7628).  So the information is there in time; it is asked too late.
SHAPE: ONE accessor for "the built-in argument rule of NAME at this token" that answers NONE when `builtin_override_target` is in force there (and the `CORE::NAME` spelling keeps the built-in), used by every one of those sites -- the name then takes the declared-user-sub path (its prototype if the replacement has one, else a list operator).  No new rule in the term parser; read docs/pexpr-term-parsing-review.md first, the sites sit in that region.
BAR: foy/k-foy-so.pl and l1..l5 as guard rows; t/op/override.t (the companion file #1870 was about) row by row; corpus-diff expected IDENTICAL apart from files that override a built-in (name them); the sweep.
NOT FIXABLE, by construction: a replacement whose NAME or PROTOTYPE only running code knows (`*{$name} = ...` with a computed name; `time % 2 ? sub ($) {...} : sub ($$) {...}`; `BEGIN { Module->import }`, #2053).
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, residue of the builtin-override work #1870): a REPLACED built-in receives the BUILT-IN\x27s argument count -- `BEGIN { *CORE::GLOBAL::rand = sub (;$$) {...} }  rand(undef, 5)` passes ONE argument, the LAST (5); brian d foy\x27s Stack Overflow program 4093822 differs from perl in every block; plus a DEFAULT-export override is not seen, and a CORE::GLOBAL replacement reads `wantarray` wrongly in a scalar slot
